title: Merge Intervals
prompt: Given an array of `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [start, end]`, merge all overlapping intervals and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input, sorted by start.

examples.explanation: [1,3] and [2,6] overlap, so they merge into [1,6].
Intervals that touch at an endpoint count as overlapping.

hints: Sort the intervals by start value first — overlaps can then only happen between neighbors.
Walk the sorted list keeping a 'current merged interval'. If the next interval's start is <= the current merged end, extend the merge; otherwise push the current merged interval and start a new one.
Don't forget to push the last merged interval after the loop ends.

solution.approach: Sort intervals by start. Keep a running merged interval, initialized to the first. For each subsequent interval, if its start is <= the running interval's end, extend the end to the max of the two ends. Otherwise, the running interval is finalized — push it and start a new running interval from the current one. Push the final running interval after the loop.
